rule: Release the issue's claim (restore the trigger label or move it to a visible blocked state) whenever a runner parks work without running it, and make the parked comment describe what actually re-triggers the work.
why: A parked issue stayed claimed with its trigger label removed and no sweep re-listed it, so it would never run even though the comment promised it would.

rule: Validate owner/repo and issue numbers parsed from issue bodies against a strict allowlist pattern, rejecting '.' and '..' segments, before interpolating them into any gh api path.
why: Unvalidated body-derived refs such as '../..#5' let an untrusted issue author redirect authenticated API calls to other endpoints or repositories.

rule: Memoize dependency-graph traversals per node with visited/visiting marking, and enforce depth, node, and concurrency caps that fail closed when exceeded.
why: Per-path recursion over author-linked issues reached roughly 10^11 paths, which would hang the gate while the issue stayed claimed.

rule: Apply the readiness gate on every path that can start work, including spec-advanced and carried-over issue ids, not only the primary listing.
why: A blocked issue was specced, parked, and then re-added from the spec-advanced carry-over and built anyway, because that path skipped the gate.

rule: Only let trusted root-issue data produce invalid, error, or failed results; content from other issue bodies must be ignored or treated as a leaf.
why: Any outside author who edits a dependency body could park trusted issues in needs-info or turn the scheduled sweep red with a non-zero exit.

rule: Track visited dependency nodes by identity and count distinct issues against the walk cap, so shared nodes are not refetched or double-counted.
why: Diamond-shaped dependency graphs were refetched and counted as extra visits, tripping the node cap and sending valid chains to needs-info.

rule: Do not edit files under .github/workflows or templates/github to wire new secrets or env; describe the exact edit (declare the secret in workflow_call.secrets, map it into the step env, update the callers) in the PR body for a human to appl…
why: The App credential shipped unreachable because the reusable workflows never declared or mapped its secrets, and the PR body omitted the hand edits that CLAUDE.md requires.

rule: When a preferred credential fails to mint, fall back to the next configured credential inside the resolver, and derive any logged credential label from the credential actually used.
why: A failed App mint silently dropped to the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN, so factory PRs got no CI while the logs still claimed the App token.

rule: Request only the GitHub App permissions the code actually uses, and keep the documented permission list identical to the permissions constant in code.
why: An unused issues:write scope made minting fail for Apps without Issues access and contradicted both the docs and the stated least-privilege intent.

rule: When a function gains a default that makes network or container calls, inject a stub for that dependency or disable its switch in the shared test options for every existing test that reaches that function.
why: Existing doctor tests reached the real npm registry because they did not stub the new default, so the suite became network-dependent and could time out on slow links.

rule: Throw on non-OK upstream responses instead of resolving to undefined, and never cache a failure result as if it were a successful lookup.
why: A single transient registry error resolved to undefined and was stored for the full cache TTL, so the hub kept reporting a lookup failure for an hour.

rule: Use `Refs #N` instead of `Closes #N` in the PR body whenever the PR does not deliver every item the linked issue or PR title names, such as a UI or action.
why: Using `Closes` would auto-close the issue even though the headline Update button and its UI were missing from the diff.

rule: Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and the affected tests locally before pushing, and delete any helper or variable the change no longer uses.
why: An unused test helper failed `pnpm lint`, which CI's `pnpm verify` runs, so the PR was blocked on a gate the author could have run locally.

rule: Substitute or remove every placeholder token (such as `YOUR_APP_SLUG`) in generated templates, and add a test that fails if any placeholder survives `apply`.
why: An unreplaced `YOUR_APP_SLUG[bot]` shipped as a live entry in every generated revise gate, and the existing test only checked the `YOUR_LOGIN` placeholder, so nothing caught it.

rule: Verify a test's or comment's premise against the base branch's current workflow files before asserting it, and state the real constraint (such as a lagging `@v1` tag) in the comment.
why: A new test asserted that no reusable workflow declared the App secret, but the base branch already declared and mapped it, so the test blocked the template change that would have made the feature work.

rule: Normalise CRLF to LF on both the pasted PR-body text and the manifest string before any substring comparison against human-edited content.
why: Browser-edited PR bodies use CRLF while manifest JSON uses LF, so multi-line items never match and a correctly pasted item stays missing forever.

rule: Escape or defang any manifest- or agent-supplied text before embedding it in a generated PR-body block, and locate block boundaries with markers that such text cannot reproduce.
why: Unescaped ids and descriptions let a reporter forge the human-paste boundary, so a block could be marked discharged with nothing pasted.

rule: Run PR-body state updates before any early return that skips the push, not only on the pushed-commit path.
why: Discharge ran only after a pushed commit, so a human who pasted the fix with no other code feedback never saw the disclosure update.

rule: When concatenating per-repository results into one combined list, sort the merged list by its timestamp (newest first) before returning it, and add a test that uses at least two repositories.
why: Each repository's results were appended in config order, so the newest run from a later repository was buried below older runs from an earlier one.

rule: Do not add a source file whose name differs from an existing file only by letter case, and check for case-only collisions before creating any new module.
why: A case-only duplicate (RepoFilter.tsx beside repoFilter.ts) resolves to different files on case-insensitive macOS and case-sensitive Linux, so it breaks on one platform while CI stays green.

rule: When one operation fans out across repositories, enforce a shared budget for expensive calls such as comment fetches and external CLI invocations across the whole fan-out, not a separate limit per repository.
why: A per-repository cap multiplied by the repository count produced roughly 16 concurrent gh processes on every refresh, exhausting the API quota the factory shares.

rule: When loading a persisted store, treat a present but invalid file as an error to surface, create defaults only when the file is absent, and never overwrite an existing file without a successful, non-clobbering backup.
why: A single malformed entry made the loader return undefined, so the next startup replaced teams.json with a bare default team and discarded hand-added teams and memberships without a log line.

rule: Keep read-only RPC handlers free of disk writes: compute derived state in memory at read time and persist only on explicit mutations.
why: list_teams and get_team rewrote teams.json whenever the project list had drifted, so on a read-only config volume they failed with EACCES even though the answer could be computed in memory.

rule: Keep pending sign-in state in a form that unauthenticated requests cannot evict: make the state stateless (an HMAC over nonce and expiry, bound to the browser cookie), or refuse new states at the cap instead of deleting unexpired ones.
why: Anonymous requests filled a bounded map and evicted in-flight states, so legitimate OAuth callbacks returned 400 and users were locked out of sign-in.

rule: Remove secrets from process.env once they are read, and register them for redaction before any child process is spawned.
why: The OAuth client secret stayed in the environment and was inherited by every spawned child process and its output, exposing it beyond the code that needed it.

rule: For every cookie-authenticated route, add negative tests for a foreign or missing Origin and for an invalid or expired session, not only the happy path.
why: Tests only sent the valid Origin, so a reorder of the auth and same-origin checks could silently allow cross-site requests carrying the session cookie.

rule: Redact persisted run output using the secret environment names registered at render or write time, not a snapshot taken before the run registers its provider keys.
why: A snapshot taken at run-accepted missed custom provider keys registered later in the run, so an opaque key echoed in a warning or run-error was written to the log in cleartext on the first run.

rule: Route every write failure in a persisted event log to the log's failure handler, which emits a warning and marks the log dead, instead of swallowing the rejection.
why: Swallowed append errors (ENOSPC, EIO, EACCES) left silent holes that the reader reported as a complete, untruncated history, contradicting the documented warning behaviour.

rule: Locate a run's persisted event log by an identifier written into the run record itself, not by the nearest timestamp at or before the record.
why: Nearest-timestamp matching returned another run's events for records that had no log of their own, such as CLI runs, failed log opens, or remote records.

rule: Before committing a base merge, treat any conflicted path that matches the CI-config (workflow) patterns as unresolvable and hold for a human, so the agent round never runs into the workflow guard.
why: A conflicted workflow file written into the worktree makes the sync-back throw an uncaught guard error, which spends the agent round and leaves the PR labelled as still revising with no comment.

rule: Reply to and resolve a review thread only when the round produced a diff that addresses that thread; a merge-only push must report zero addressed items and leave threads open.
why: Pushing a merge commit with no agent change while replying 'Addressed in commit' and resolving every thread misreports unaddressed feedback as fixed.

rule: Run the conflict-marker check immediately before the diff capture and push, after the repair loop, so repair passes cannot reintroduce markers unnoticed.
why: A repair pass that restores a conflicted file after the one-time marker check lets markers be pushed while the summary still reports the conflicts as resolved.

rule: When a change alters how a deployment mode or launch flow is selected, update every doc, compose example, and container config that describes the old flow in the same change, and mark the change as breaking.
why: Without it, existing container and reverse-proxy operators followed docs that no longer worked, and the hub stopped serving its web UI on upgrade with no escape hatch.

rule: Before delegating an unauthenticated route to a third-party auth handler, enforce a request body-size cap and set the handler's rate limiting explicitly rather than relying on library defaults.
why: Without it, anonymous clients could send oversized POSTs and flood the auth database with OAuth-state rows, because the defaults were unverified and rate limiting was off.

rule: Read secret environment variables once at startup, delete them from process.env, and add their names to the secret-scan list.
why: Without it, secrets stayed in process.env where every spawned child process inherited them and the outgoing-diff secret scan did not catch the leak.

rule: Name any persisted per-run artifact from an identifier the client already receives, and return that identifier in the run's events or listing so clients can address it.
why: The log was named from a timestamp no API exposed, so reads for every run except a task's newest returned silent empty pages.

rule: Do not await disk I/O on the path that releases a shared run slot; finish and dequeue the run first, or bound the write with a timeout.
why: A stalled volume write kept the slot marked active, so finishRun and startNext never ran and every queued run waited indefinitely.

rule: Re-assert state-path and symlink safety before every file write instead of caching the result from the first write.
why: Checking once and caching the path let a later symlink swap redirect appends outside the checkout, unlike the per-append check in appendMetric.

rule: Before force-pushing a rebased branch, require that every path differing between the rebased HEAD and the clean merge tree is among the files the agent was shown as conflicted, otherwise reset and hold.
why: Files that conflicted only at an intermediate replay stop were silently resolved to the branch's version, reverting base changes that would land on the base branch when the PR merged.

rule: When checking authorship or ownership across a branch's commit range, include merge commits instead of filtering them out with `--no-merges`.
why: A human merge commit carrying a hand conflict resolution passed the factory-ownership check, was then flattened by the rebase, and was force-pushed over.

rule: When a lease-protected or force push fails after the agent has run, post the failure as a PR comment and clear the in-progress label rather than letting the error fall into the generic catch.
why: A rejected push left the PR labelled as revising with no notice, so every round would run the agent and then fail silently.

rule: Validate any URL read from a run record or imported artifact by requiring a string type, parsing it with `new URL`, requiring the `https:` protocol, rejecting username or password, capping its length, and returning the normalized `href`.
why: Without these checks, non-string values passed through as links, userinfo hosts were labelled with a brand they never matched, and very long slash runs could block the hub's event loop.

rule: When `main` has changed files under `.github/workflows/`, rebase the branch onto `main` instead of merging it.
why: A merge left conflicts in workflow files that the push token could not resolve, so the branch stayed unmergeable until it was rebased.

rule: Add a test asserting the rendered href and label for every new user-visible link and every new server-side URL mapping before the change is considered complete.
why: Links shipped without tests for the run list, run detail, GitLab `web_url` mapping and Linear `url` mapping, so regressions in those paths would go unnoticed.

rule: Serialize every read-modify-write of a persisted credential or config file through a single promise chain, and give each temp file a unique name.
why: Overlapping set and delete calls read the same snapshot, so the last rename silently drops another entry after a success response, and a shared temp name makes renames fail with ENOENT.

rule: Before overwriting or deleting a secret value that the outgoing-secret scanner reads from process.env, register the displaced value with the redaction list.
why: Rotating a key while a run is in flight removes the old value from the exact-match scan, so that run can publish the old key unredacted.

rule: When storing an override for a provider credential, enumerate every environment variable the resolver checks for that provider in precedence order, and override or report all of them.
why: Writing only OPENAI_API_KEY leaves CODEX_API_KEY or CODEX_AUTH_JSON taking precedence, so Settings shows the key as set while runs keep using the old one.

rule: When a setting decides how CI or a runner behaves, store it in a tracked file or read it from the base ref, never from a git-ignored working-tree file.
why: A git-ignored config is absent in CI checkouts, so the CI run silently uses different defaults and refuses or retargets cards that the board showed as valid.

rule: Apply the same validation rules to a shared config value on every write path, including the Tauri command and the hub RPC.
why: When only one write path validated the branch name, an unsafe value saved through the other path later refused every unlabelled run.

rule: Reset form selection state (such as a target branch) when its project, options, or dialog session changes, so a hidden stale value is never submitted.
why: A previously chosen branch survived cancel, reopen, or project switch and was sent while the select displayed a different option, so the card targeted a branch the user could not see.

rule: Before wiring any self-update or installer path, confirm it cannot exit the app, overwrite a running sidecar, or leave child runs orphaned, and gate it on the hub reporting no active runs.
why: Without that check, installing an update can kill in-flight runs and replace files the running hub still uses, even though the UI told the user it would not.

rule: When adding a Rust dependency, run cargo build and commit the updated Cargo.lock in the same change.
why: Without a resolved lockfile the new code is never compiled in CI, and transitive crates float unpinned into a release job that holds signing secrets.

rule: Keep landing and README claims true on main, and link only to releases or features that already exist.
why: Without this, a Download button can point at a release that 404s until a maintainer publishes it, and the breakage ships with the next manual deploy.

rule: Trim and normalise input before running redaction or pattern matches on it, and assert the redaction holds for padded values, not only clean ones.
why: Anchored URL detectors missed a credential-bearing clone URL with leading whitespace, so the raw userinfo was written to the audit log while the clone still succeeded.

rule: Validate client-supplied and on-disk fields with the same type guard on both write and read before they are persisted or rendered, as sibling fields already are.
why: An unvalidated startedBy was persisted on the non-hub path and forwarded unchecked on read, so a non-string value could blank the Runs table and let any file writer forge attribution.

rule: When adding a state-changing hub RPC, either add it to the audit allowlist or state its exemption, and make the docs coverage claim match the actual list.
why: docs/hub.md claimed every state-changing action was audited, but spawn_run, kill_run and several draft writes were absent from AUDITED, so the documented guarantee overstated coverage.

rule: When filtering or routing published events by payload fields, derive the filter from the exact payload shape each publisher emits (including string and nested payloads), and add a test that subscribes as a restricted user and asserts that p…
why: The team filter matched only top-level repoPath/path objects, so no real event passed it and team members lost all live run and change updates while the filter had no test.

rule: When adding an authorization layer to an RPC dispatcher, enumerate every command in the catalogue and gate each one explicitly, including commands that look read-only, fleet-wide, or side-effecting on the host.
why: Commands such as browse_dirs, agent_cli_versions and api_cancel_complete were missed, so signed-in users outside any team could still reach host or cross-team functionality.

rule: When refusing access to a resource in a multi-tenant hub, return one identical, path-free message for unknown, unregistered and foreign resources.
why: Distinct refusal texts that echo paths let a member enumerate which repositories and run ids exist on the host and belong to other teams.

rule: When selecting which review's blocking findings to address, match the review marker to the PR's current head SHA and ignore markers from earlier heads.
why: Without this, revision rounds answer stale findings from older reviews, so the loop keeps cycling without clearing the findings on the code that is actually under review.

rule: When the base branch has changed CI configuration, rebase the branch onto the base and push with a lease-protected force push instead of merging the base in.
why: Merging the base failed because the push token may not write CI-config changes into the branch, which forced an extra rebase round.

rule: Keep a stated BLOCKING verdict whenever its file cannot be matched to the changed-file list, and treat a truncated diff as unknown rather than as an empty change set.
why: Unmatched file names and truncated diffs let the host downgrade valid blocking findings to a clean verdict, which bypasses the gate.

rule: Extract the review verdict and the re-review block only from the first non-blank line or a fixed position, never from text inside quotes or code fences.
why: Verdict text matched anywhere in the reply let quoted or fenced content override the reviewer's real verdict.

rule: When overriding Vitest `test.exclude` in a config, spread `configDefaults.exclude` (for example `[...configDefaults.exclude, 'e2e/**']`) instead of replacing the list.
why: Replacing the default exclude drops the nested `**/node_modules/**` pattern, so bundled dependency test files get collected and a local `pnpm test` can run them.

rule: Scope responsive layout changes to their breakpoint with `max-md:` (or equivalent) variants rather than applying flex-wrap or similar changes at every width.
why: An unconditional `flex-wrap` on the Needs-you header regressed the desktop layout, where long titles now drop to their own line instead of truncating.

rule: When adding a new test directory or Playwright spec, wire it into a CI or verify gate and typecheck it (add it to tsconfig or a lint step), and run the spec before claiming its assertions hold.
why: A new e2e spec that no gate runs or typechecks can fail on its first real step, leaving the claimed 390 px coverage unverified and free to rot.

rule: When a config field is superseded by a newer field, resolve it through a single shared resolver (new field, then validated legacy field) that every reader calls, including aggregators, settings UI, and board or task-creation code, rather th…
why: Readers that consulted only the new field showed existing projects under the wrong tracker, and separate copies of the fallback logic drifted apart.

rule: When a stored setting can be absent, give its select or picker an explicit empty option that represents the unset state, and never display a default value the config does not actually hold.
why: A select that showed GitHub for an unset config never fired a change event when the user re-selected it, so the value the board required was never saved and Save stayed disabled.

rule: Authorize team roles and visibility only on server-controlled, immutable identity (user id or provider-verified e-mail), and make authentication-library fields that feed authorization non-writable by the client, for example with `input: fal…
why: A signed-in user could post a forged `providerLogin` to `/api/auth/update-user` and gain admin rights over any team that listed that login.

rule: Pass the selected team or scope id to every server call that returns scoped data (projects, runs, tasks, needs-you items) and refetch when it changes, rather than fetching unscoped and filtering in the browser.
why: Without the id the server returns the user's first team's data, so switching teams shows the wrong or an empty list.

rule: Before writing code or docs that call hub RPC commands or describe access rules, confirm the command names, identity matching, and guards in the checked-out source, and do not rely on the issue title or on an assumed base.
why: The branch used command names and access rules that did not exist in the tree, so the UI called missing commands and the docs described behaviour the code did not implement.

rule: Never grant command or window permissions to wildcard remote origins such as http://*/* or https://*/*; scope each remote capability to a specific, validated origin.
why: A wildcard remote grant lets any page the window loads, including link targets and identity-provider redirects, call privileged commands and read or alter saved state.

rule: Reject glob or pattern metacharacters (*, (, ), {, }) and any host outside plain [a-z0-9.-] or a bracketed IPv6 literal before a user-supplied URL is turned into a capability URL pattern.
why: Unvalidated input such as https://* parses as a valid URL, so it silently becomes a wildcard grant persisted across launches.

rule: Enforce permission checks in the backend or capability configuration, never only in frontend UI conditionals such as hiding a button.
why: A UI-only check such as hiding Add for non-loopback pages is presentation only, so any page can still invoke the underlying command.

rule: Derive admin or authorization identity only from server-verified provider account data, never from user-writable profile or auth-update fields.
why: A member who rewrote a stored user-writable field before it was disabled could pass the admin check and change the instance credential and policy for everyone.

rule: When registering a structured secret for redaction, also register each parsed inner secret value (token fields, API keys) individually, not only the whole blob.
why: Redaction and the outgoing-diff gate matched only the full stored JSON, so inner tokens could leak into PR bodies, comments, logs, and delivered diffs.

rule: For a user-only credential run, strip every key environment variable the run's provider choice can read, and refuse the run when the user has no credential for that provider.
why: Stripping only a fixed list of names let custom providers and gateway base URLs fall through to the instance key while the run was recorded as user-credentialed.

rule: Before re-publishing a change that touches apps/desktop, run the desktop CI steps (`pnpm test:desktop` and `pnpm --dir apps/desktop build`) in addition to the root `pnpm run verify`.
why: Root verify does not cover apps/desktop, so a required prop missing from new tests passed the proof of work and then failed CI's desktop typecheck and tests.

rule: Derive a card's live state (running stage, repair count, receipt, PR link) from the live stage marker, and never from the last delivered run record.
why: Run records are written only at delivery, so a re-running card showed the previous run's receipt, PR link and repair note.

rule: When a UI needs only run summary facts, read them with the artifact-free reader (records and proof) rather than the reader that includes diffs and transcripts.
why: Opening a card downloaded every stage's diff and transcript over hub HTTP just to render a handful of facts.

rule: Before requesting review, merge the current base branch into the feature branch and run `pnpm test:desktop` and `pnpm --dir apps/desktop build`, not only the root verify.
why: The branch fell behind main twice, which produced textual conflicts in App.tsx and broke a CI-run desktop demo test and the desktop build that the root verify does not cover.

rule: Do not poll gh-backed hub endpoints on a fixed short interval in every tab; poll on demand, pause while `document.hidden`, use a long interval, or add a hub-side cache.
why: A 30-second interval running the uncached needs-you read in every open tab multiplies GitHub CLI and GraphQL calls on the shared quota.

rule: Build tab UIs with the shared `Tabs` components from `@/ui` instead of hand-rolling role=tablist and role=tab buttons.
why: Hand-rolled tabs lacked arrow-key navigation, tabpanel and aria-controls wiring, and diverged from how RunDetail already implements tabs.

rule: Do not derive Inspector load effect dependencies or refetch triggers from the current screen; use a screen-independent flag so moving between screens neither resets state nor refetches.
why: A screen-dependent allRepos flag re-ran the Inspector load effect on every Board/Runs and Settings/New Task move, overwriting the live-run focus and refetching all runs.

rule: Merge the latest main into the branch before changing navigation or screen names, and keep main's screen set rather than reintroducing removed screens or old filter APIs.
why: The branch conflicted with main after the navigation change landed, which forced a revision round to reconcile removed screens and replaced repository-filter names.

rule: Keep remote tracker calls off the synchronous list-response path, and cache their promises and failures so concurrent or repeated requests share one read.
why: Runs listing now awaits per-repository tracker reads with no in-flight dedupe and no failure caching, so opening Runs stalls on many calls and repeats failing calls on every refresh.

rule: Derive every task-id or run-record lookup key from the exact expression the producer uses (for example `spec-<slug>-<N>` and `revise-pr-<slug>-<PR>`), and build test records through the producer rather than hand-typed id literals.
why: Hand-typed test ids matched an id shape no runner emits, so real spec and revise records were silently dropped from the audit view and the review blocked the PR.

rule: Before treating a task's numeric suffix as a GitHub issue number, check the tracker prefix and query GitHub only for `gh-` ids.
why: Taking trailing digits from any taskId made a Linear or GitLab card display the history of an unrelated GitHub issue.

rule: Include a PR in an issue's history only when a run record or a closing reference links it to that issue, never on a textual mention alone.
why: Any same-repo PR that merely mentioned the issue had its merge and review verdicts merged into that issue's history, so outsiders could shape the audit record.

rule: Derive any value that gets persisted or later executed from server-side state, and reject a client-echoed value that differs from the server's derivation before writing.
why: Persisting the client-supplied repo slug let one hub user set the secret target shown to other users, which was a blocking security finding.

rule: Validate a record against the same rules before writing it, and derive hosts and URL patterns from configuration instead of hard-coding github.com.
why: Records that the reader later rejects were written anyway, so the dialog silently showed a "never started" state with no PR link and no error on self-hosted GitHub.

rule: Pass the store's config directory through the context object (ctx.configDir) to every hub store instead of reading process environment variables.
why: The checklist store read the process environment, so demo runs wrote into the user's real config directory and tests had to mutate process.env without restoring it.

rule: After editing apps/desktop/src/wire.ts or src/wire.ts, regenerate the mirrored copy and run the root wire drift guard (src/wire.test.ts) before handing off.
why: The desktop wire copy drifted from the generator output, so the PR's recorded verify run failed and the change could not be shown to pass.

rule: When changing files under apps/desktop, run that package's own typecheck and test suite (`tsc` and `vitest run` in apps/desktop) in addition to root `pnpm run verify`.
why: Root verify does not typecheck or test the desktop app, so the desktop changes had no recorded green run and CI could still fail after merge.
